agent.save_to_tutorial_notes("To create a pivot table in LibreOffice Calc:\n1. Position the cursor within a range of cells containing values, row and column headings.\n2. Choose Insert - Pivot Table. The Select Source dialogue box appears. Choose Current selection and confirm with OK. The table headers are shown as buttons in the Pivot Table dialogue box. Drag these buttons as required and drop them into the layout areas \"Filters\", \"Column Fields\", \"Row Fields\" and \"Data Fields\".\n3. Drag the desired buttons into one of the four areas. Drag a button to the Filters area to create a button and a list box on top of the generated pivot table. The list box can be used to filter the pivot table by the contents of the selected item. You can use drag-and-drop within the generated pivot table to use another page field as a filter. If the button is dropped in the Data Fields area it will be used to calculate the data.\n4. By double-clicking on one of the fields in the Data Fields area you can call up the Data Field dialogue box.\n5. Use the Data Field dialog to select the calculations to be used for the data. To make a multiple selection, press the Ctrl key while clicking the desired calculation.\n6. The order of the buttons can be changed at any time by moving them to a different position in the area with the mouse.\n7. Remove a button by dragging it back to the area of the other buttons at the right of the dialogue box.\n8. To open the Data Field dialogue box, double-click one of the buttons in the Row Fields or Column Fields area. Use the dialogue box to select if and to what extent LibreOffice calculates display subtotals.\n9. Exit the Pivot Table dialogue box by clicking OK. A Filter button will now be inserted, or a page button for every data field that you dropped in the Filters area. The pivot table is inserted.")

The command would be:\n   ```bash\n   cp -R /home/administrator/practice/ /home/administrator/Downloads/new3/\n   ```\n\n5. **Behavior Based on Destination Directory**:\n   - If the destination directory does not exist, `cp` creates it and copies the content of the source directory recursively.\n   - If the destination directory already exists, the copy of the source directory becomes a sub-directory under the destination directory.\n\n6. **Verify the Copy**: Use the `ls` command to display all the files in the destination directory to confirm the successful copy.\n   ```bash\n   ls /home/administrator/Downloads/new3/\n   ```")

For example, copy the `ls` command and its dependencies:\n   ```bash\n   sudo cp /bin/ls /home/username/web/\n   sudo ldd /bin/ls\n   ```\n   Copy the listed libraries to the appropriate location in the chroot environment.\n\n5. Set the correct permissions for the chroot directory:\n   ```bash\n   sudo chown root:root /home/username/web\n   sudo chmod 755 /home/username/web\n   ```\n\n6. Configure SSH to use the chroot environment. Edit the SSH configuration file:\n   ```bash\n   sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config\n   ```\n   Add the following lines:\n   ```bash\n   Match User username\n       ChrootDirectory /home/username/web\n       ForceCommand internal-sftp\n       AllowTcpForwarding no\n       X11Forwarding no\n   ```\n\n7.
